official_measurement_examples.name: New July 2026 toolkit
official_measurement_examples.fact: MHCLG published a Local Green Space neighbourhood-plan toolkit on 24 July 2026, but the page explicitly says the toolkit has not yet been updated to reflect recent planning-policy changes and should be treated as background alongside current policy.

official_measurement_examples.name: National dataset coverage gap
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data currently reports 0 Local Green Space records, 0 providers and no collection attempt; this is a collection gap and cannot be used as evidence that a location has no Local Green Space designation.

official_measurement_examples.name: Designation timing
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current NPPF says Local Green Space should only be designated when a local or neighbourhood plan is prepared or updated and should be capable of enduring beyond the end of the plan period.

official_measurement_examples.name: Designation criteria
official_measurement_examples.fact: NPPF requires Local Green Space to be close to the community, demonstrably special with local significance and local in character rather than an extensive tract of land.

official_measurement_examples.name: Management policy
official_measurement_examples.fact: Development within Local Green Space is managed consistently with national Green Belt policy, but Local Green Space is a distinct designation and must not be relabelled as Green Belt.

official_measurement_examples.name: Open-space distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning practice guidance treats open space broadly, including many spaces of public value; an open-space record is not automatically a Local Green Space designation.

official_measurement_examples.name: Plan status
official_measurement_examples.fact: Neighbourhood and local-plan evidence must retain whether a plan is current, emerging, historical, made or under review; a proposed designation is not automatically an adopted designation.

official_measurement_examples.name: Environmental screening separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Strategic Environmental Assessment or Habitats screening for a neighbourhood plan is a separate process from designating an individual Local Green Space and does not grant parcel development permission.

core_rules: zero national Local Green Space records is a data-coverage gap not proof of no designation
Local Green Space must retain its local or neighbourhood plan source
proposed and adopted Local Green Space designations must remain distinct
Local Green Space is not the same designation as Green Belt
generic open space is not automatically Local Green Space
Local Green Space criteria require more than geometric proximity
a Local Green Space designation is not a cadastral ownership boundary
Local Green Space status does not itself determine development yield
new July 2026 toolkit carries an explicit policy-transition caveat
current NPPF policy takes precedence over outdated toolkit assumptions
neighbourhood-plan status and dates must be retained
SEA/HRA screening is distinct from Local Green Space designation
absence from Planning Data is not absence from local plan documents
open-space policy does not itself grant public access or ownership rights
no parcel Local Green Space clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
